content: where the functions $K = top\_k(G)$ gets the indices of the top $k$ vectors in $G$ and $P = sparse\_vector(K,0,-\infty )$ creates a sparse vector where the values of $K$ is 0 and $-\infty $ otherwise. The sparse vector $P$ is added to the original importance score vector $G$ to create a new importance score vector. In this new vector, important scores of non-top $k$0 entities are $k$1 . When softmax is applied, this gives very small, negligible, and close-to-zero values to non-top $k$2 entities. The value $k$3 depends on the lengths of the input text and summary. Moreover, when $k$4 increases towards infinity, firm attention becomes soft attention. We decide $k$5 empirically (see Section "Experimental settings" ).
